clue.text: Such news could appear to be nothing, having no purpose

definitions.text: Such news could appear to be nothing
definitions.meaning: NEWS is made of the four compass points N, E, W, S; take those directions away and nothing is left
lacking any aim or sense of where one is going

explanation.definitionFit: Something aimless has no sense of where it is heading, the figurative sense of lacking a course.

clue.text: Critical factor put off male worker — having to go outside home

parts.note: to put off is to deter

indicators.note: the male worker pair surrounds the word for home

parts.note: the ant is the crossword's usual worker insect
IN means at home

explanation.surface: An employee is discouraged from working because he must leave the house.
explanation.walkthrough: The dash makes the worker look like the subject of the surface; 'having to go outside' wraps the male worker round home.
explanation.definitionFit: A determinant is a factor that decides an outcome, so a critical factor.

clue.text: Ugly sight? Not the female fair!

indicators.note: says the following letter is to be left out of the ugly sight word

parts.note: a fright is a person or thing of grotesque appearance

explanation.surface: Someone remarks that a woman at the fair is no beauty.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not the female' drops F from FRIGHT. 'Fair' looks like a beautiful woman but means just or proper.
explanation.definitionFit: Fair and right both mean just or proper, as in a fair decision.

clue.text: What could have made Cash croon sad songs?

indicators.note: asks what the letters of the two words could be rearranged into

explanation.surface: A question about what made the country singer Johnny Cash sing mournful ballads.
explanation.walkthrough: 'What could have made' asks for the letters of CASH CROON rearranged. Coronachs are Scottish and Irish funeral laments.
explanation.definitionFit: A coronach is a Highland or Irish dirge, a lament sung at funerals.

clue.text: It looks as if I've got up to P for Painting

parts.note: I'M, short for I am, stands in for I've here, both being contractions about the speaker
reaching P in the alphabet means having gone past O

explanation.surface: Someone working through an alphabetical list of art terms says they have reached the letter P.
explanation.walkthrough: Read the answer as I'M PAST O: having got up to P, you are past O. 'It looks as if' tells you to read it that way.
explanation.definitionFit: Impasto is a technique of laying paint on thickly, a kind of painting.

clue.text: Retreats with lack of any sign of approval

parts.note: NO means not any
an OK is a sign of approval; plural here

explanation.surface: Someone withdraws because nobody ever gives them a nod of approval.
explanation.definitionFit: Nooks are secluded corners, places one can retreat to.

clue.text: Fanatic wants more, endlessly troubled times

indicators.note: the word for more loses its final letter

parts.note: extra means more

indicators.note: troubled letters are stirred up and rearranged

explanation.surface: A zealot keeps demanding more during difficult times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'endlessly' cuts EXTRA to EXTR; 'troubled' turns TIMES into EMIST.
explanation.definitionFit: An extremist holds fanatical views, going to the far edge of an opinion.

clue.text: Not much money? One's endlessly bitter

indicators.note: the word for bitter loses its final letter

parts.note: sour means bitter in taste

explanation.surface: Someone short of cash is perpetually resentful.
explanation.walkthrough: A sou was an old French coin of small value, hence a trifling amount.
explanation.definitionFit: A sou was a low-value French coin, so the word stands for very little money.

clue.text: Animal trapped in direst agony

indicators.note: the letters are caught across the words that follow

explanation.surface: A creature is caught in a trap and suffering terribly.
explanation.definitionFit: A stag is a male deer, an example of an animal.

clue.text: Record-keeper gets to criticise doorman outside university

parts.note: to rap is to criticise sharply

indicators.note: the doorman word goes round the letter for university

parts.note: a porter guards a door

explanation.surface: A secretary scolds the college porter.
explanation.walkthrough: 'outside' wraps the doorman round the university letter; 'gets to' is just a link.
explanation.definitionFit: A rapporteur is a person appointed to record and report a committee's proceedings.

clue.text: Not-half-attractive nurses in poses

indicators.note: only half the word for attractive is kept, the second half going

parts.note: pretty means attractive
to nurse is to tend

explanation.surface: Plain-looking nurses strike poses.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Not-half' keeps only the front half, PRET. 'poses' is a verb here, to put on a show, not the noun it seems.
explanation.definitionFit: To pose as something is to pretend, to feign a role.

clue.text: Cylindrical piece that may have an internal radius

definitions.text: Cylindrical piece that may have an internal radius

parts.words: Cylindrical piece that may have an internal radius
parts.note: reads like engineering jargon for a tube's inner measurement, but the radius is the forearm bone inside a garment's tube of cloth

explanation.definitionFit: A sleeve is both a cylindrical engineering part and the arm of a garment, which encloses the radius bone.

clue.text: Dressing in something feathery with very little on top

parts.note: V is the abbreviation for very, a little bit of it
an aigrette is a plume of feathers worn as an ornament

explanation.surface: Someone is dressed in a feathered costume with barely anything covering the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'on top' in a down entry means the very-little letter comes first; 'in' is taken literally rather than as a container.
explanation.definitionFit: Vinaigrette is an oil and vinegar salad dressing.

clue.text: It could mean Queen will take the flak in part of London

definitions.text: It could mean Queen will take the flak
definitions.meaning: if the monarch's husband is angry, his wife bears the brunt
a district and major railway station in north London

explanation.definitionFit: King's Cross is a district of north London around the main-line station of that name.

clue.text: Piano hit picking up all the top prizes

parts.note: a grand is a grand piano
to slam is to hit hard

explanation.surface: A pianist's hit song sweeps all the awards.
explanation.walkthrough: A grand slam is winning all the major titles in a sport such as tennis or golf.
explanation.definitionFit: Grand slam means winning every major championship in a season, so taking all top prizes.

clue.text: Namely, a vindictive type who's out to get what he can?

definitions.text: who's out to get what he can

parts.note: SC is short for scilicet, Latin for namely
an avenger seeks revenge

explanation.surface: A vengeful person is described as an opportunist on the make.
explanation.definitionFit: A scavenger collects whatever can be salvaged, taking what others leave.

clue.text: It's said I possess a place of spiritual retreat

indicators.note: says the words are spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: I possess a means I own a

explanation.surface: Someone claims to own a religious retreat.
explanation.walkthrough: Iona is a Hebridean island where St Columba founded a monastery; it remains a retreat centre.
explanation.definitionFit: The Scottish island of Iona houses an abbey and community used for spiritual retreats.

clue.text: A joke about being dotty

indicators.note: turns the pair of words back to front

parts.note: a gag is a joke

explanation.surface: A joke concerning someone eccentric.
explanation.walkthrough: 'about' reverses AGAG to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Gaga and dotty both mean slightly mad or senile, in informal speech.

clue.text: ""Tis the man on the bridge" — anapaestic, could that be?

indicators.note: asks whether the word's letters could be rearranged into the answer

explanation.surface: A line of verse is scanned for its metre, the speaker wondering if it is anapaestic.
explanation.walkthrough: 'could that be' points to the letters of ANAPAESTIC rearranged. The bridge is a ship's command platform.
explanation.definitionFit: A ship's master commands from the bridge, the raised platform for navigation.

clue.text: Condemn a defect audibly

indicators.note: says the phrase is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a taint is a defect or blemish

explanation.surface: Someone is told to denounce a flaw out loud.
explanation.definitionFit: To attaint was to condemn someone, historically by sentence that stripped civil rights.

clue.text: Dull work good chap wants to avoid, after starting

parts.note: ST, for saint, is the crossword's good man

indicators.note: the word for avoid loses its starting letter

parts.note: to dodge is to avoid

explanation.surface: Someone tries to get out of a boring job once it has begun.
explanation.walkthrough: 'after starting' drops the opening letter of the avoid word, leaving ODGE; 'wants' is only a link.
explanation.definitionFit: Stodge is heavy, dull material, used of uninspiring work as well as food.

clue.text: Woman's fine article

parts.note: an eric was a fine paid in old Irish law for a killing
A is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A lady's elegant piece of writing.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Woman's' is Woman is: the answer is a woman's name.
explanation.definitionFit: Erica is a woman's given name.

clue.text: Bird squashing rock plant

indicators.note: the bird word presses around the rock word

parts.note: a tern is a seabird
a reef is a ridge of rock

explanation.surface: A bird crushes a plant growing on a rock.
explanation.walkthrough: 'squashing' puts the rock inside the bird. 'Bird' looks like the subject; it is the outer piece.
explanation.definitionFit: A tree fern is a large fern with a trunk-like stem, a kind of plant.

clue.text: Group with some killers amusing soldier

parts.note: fun means amusing
GI is an American soldier

explanation.surface: A gang including murderers entertains a soldier.
explanation.walkthrough: Fungi are a biological group, and some, like death caps, are deadly.
explanation.definitionFit: Fungi form a kingdom of organisms, some species of which are poisonous.

clue.text: Getting back maiden, a nice girl, well-adjusted

parts.note: M is a maiden over in cricket scoring, an over with no runs

explanation.surface: A balanced young woman is recovering.
explanation.walkthrough: 'well-adjusted' rearranges M with A NICE GIRL. A maiden is a cricket over with no runs scored.
explanation.definitionFit: Reclaiming something is getting it back.

clue.text: Creature abandoned with head chopped off

indicators.note: the word for abandoned loses its first letter

parts.note: left means abandoned

explanation.surface: A beast is left behind after being beheaded.
explanation.definitionFit: An eft is a newt, a small amphibian creature.

clue.text: On the bottom line there's a catch reportedly

indicators.note: says the word is spoken, giving a sound-alike

parts.note: a net is a catch, as of fish

explanation.surface: An accountant warns that there is a snag in the final figures.
explanation.definitionFit: Nett figures are those after deductions, the bottom line of an account.

clue.text: When illegal drinkers used to enjoy themselves repeatedly

definitions.text: When illegal drinkers used to enjoy themselves
definitions.meaning: drinking past closing time, after the pub had called time, was against the licensing law

explanation.walkthrough: British pubs once had strict closing hours, signalled by the landlord calling time.
explanation.definitionFit: The phrase means again and again, on many occasions.
